channel.title: Nodus Blog
channel.description: Notes from the Nodus project: comparisons with the tools around it, workflows worth stealing, and what is being built next.

item.title: Nodus vs NotebookLM: two different models for AI-assisted research
item.description: Nodus and NotebookLM both ground AI in the researcher’s own sources, and then diverge. One is built around the notebook. The other turns a long-term corpus into evidence, ideas and relationships that outlive the session.

item.title: How Nodus can support research in the humanities
item.description: Humanities projects rarely fit one tool: books, archival documents, photographs, interviews and datasets all belong to the same argument. Nodus keeps them in one local-first workspace, with every finding still attached to its source.

item.title: How to Organize a Large Academic Research Library
item.description: Once a project grows to hundreds of sources, the hard part is no longer storage but context: knowing why a source was collected and how it connects to your ideas.

item.title: Nodus: an open source research workspace for academic work
item.description: Research is spread across reference managers, PDF folders, note apps and chatbots. Nodus keeps sources, ideas and the evidence behind them in one local-first workspace.
